statements.text: Based in Daejon, South Korea, Hanon Systems makes heating and air conditioning systems at a plant in Shorter, Alabama, that opened in 2003 and has expanded at least three times.
A South Korean company will build a $40 million factory in coastal Georgia to make heating and cooling systems near a Hyundai Motor Group auto assembly plant.
Headquartered in Ulsan, Korea, Duckyang supplies cockpit modules to customers around the world including Hyundai, Kia, Renault Samsung Motors, Genesis, and Mobis.

Duckyang, an electric mobility parts supplier of automotive battery modules and energy storage systems to SK Battery America (SKBA), will invest $10 million in opening its first U.S. manufacturing facility in Jackson County.
Duckyang’s new 230,000-square-foot facility will be located at 984 Broadway Avenue in Braselton.
Like a number of South Korean suppliers, Hanon Systems already supplies a Hyundai assembly plant in Montgomery, Alabama, and a Kia plant in West Point, Georgia.
Hanon Systems announced Tuesday that it would build the plant in Statesboro, with plans to hire at least 160 new employees.
Content produced in North Korea is not presently allowed into the United States, a situation that the KORUS FTA would not change.
Under the proposed KORUS FTA, automakers and most component manufacturers can select one of three options for calculating regional value content.
The KORUS FTA has two specific rule of origin requirements. First, all products must be produced in either the United States or South Korea.
